sections.h2: The ladder is a step function, not a percentage
paras: Four thresholds, four fixed amounts. As a share of the order total that is 10.00% at $500.00, 13.33% at $750.00, 22.50% at $1,000.00 and 25.00% at $2,000.00. Nothing in the terms is proportional, so the only way to read the code is to know which step a cart is standing on.

$2,000.00 is the top of the ladder and also the best rate, because the page caps the amount there. The same $500.00 on a $4,000.00 order is 12.50%, and on a $5,000.00 order it is 10.00% — level with the lowest tier. Past the last threshold the code gets worse with every dollar added.

sections.h2: Where the ladder jumps: four cliffs, one dollar wide
paras: $1,999.00 takes $225.00, which is 11.26% of the order. $2,000.00 takes $500.00, which is 25.00%. One dollar more on the order is $275.00 more off, and the rate more than doubles. This is the widest step on the ladder.

The same shape repeats lower down. $999.00 takes $100.00, which is 10.01%; $1,000.00 takes $225.00, which is 22.50%, so $1 buys $125.00. $749.00 takes $50.00, which is 6.68%; $750.00 takes $100.00, which is 13.33%, so $1 buys $50.00. And $499.00 takes nothing at all, while $500.00 takes $50.00, which is 10.00%.

Read as shopping arithmetic: one dollar below $2,000.00, any item priced under $275.00 that carries a cart over the threshold leaves you paying less than the short basket would. $1,999.00 minus $225.00 is $1,774.00; $2,000.00 minus $500.00 is $1,500.00; break-even sits at an added item of exactly $275.00.
